title: Changing Remittance Terms and Credit Reporting Authorization on Contingency Placement Agreements
content:
**Rule.** A creditor client may change its remittance basis, remittance frequency or credit reporting authorization on an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements through a service request, and the change is written to the agreement once the request is processed. Terms are changed only on agreements whose status is active or placement hold; an agreement in runoff keeps its terms to the end.

## Basis of the rule, question by question

**Which options may the client choose?**
Gross remittance is available only where the tier makes gross remittance available, weekly remittance only where the tier makes weekly remittance available, and semi-monthly only where the tier makes semi-monthly remittance available.

**How many changes are allowed?**
Remittance basis and frequency changes together count against the tier's allowance of remittance basis or frequency changes per agreement year; reporting authorization changes count against the tier's allowance of credit reporting authorization changes per agreement year. Both are counted in the agreement year: from the anniversary of the effective date on or before the handling date, through the handling date, counting the agreement's processed remittance terms change requests and reporting authorization change requests respectively.

**From when does a remittance change apply?**
A remittance change applies from the first remittance period that begins at least the tier's lead days, in calendar days, after the request date.

**From when does a reporting authorization change apply?**
A reporting authorization change takes effect when processed. Revoking it stops initial reports and leads to deletion of every live tradeline on the client's accounts under the credit reporting rule; granting it lets accounts that meet the reporting rule be reported from the next cycle.

**What status must the agreement have?**
Active or placement hold, as the agreement record shows. An agreement in runoff keeps its terms to the end.

## Hypothetical cases

- A semi-monthly agreement with lead days of 10, on a tier that makes gross remittance available, asks on the 3rd to change its remittance basis from net to gross. Its remittance periods begin on the 1st and the 16th; the 16th is 13 days after the request, at least 10, so the change applies from the period beginning on the 16th.
- The same request with lead days of 15: the 16th is only 13 days after the request, so the change applies from the period beginning on the 1st of the following month.
- An agreement whose effective date is 10 April, handling date 2 March: the agreement year runs from the 10 April anniversary on or before 2 March through 2 March.
